LESSON: PRESENTATION SKILLS SPEAKING

Grade: Grade 2
Subject: LITERACY ACTIVITIES
Strand: Strand 2
Topic 2.5: Presentation skills SPEAKING

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Presentation skills SPEAKING. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: What does a good SPEAKING learner should be able to: using the learnt vocabulary presenter do?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. express self appropriately using acquired vocabulary speaking competitions to communicate effectively
2. use appropriate tonal variation, articulation and presentation skills(videos recording of stress to express self- presentations or role playing by teacher) confidently

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

• Presentation skills SPEAKING helps you communicate well at school and at home.

• Listen with your eyes and ears. Face the speaker and wait for your turn.

• When you speak, use a clear voice and polite words.

• Practise short dialogues with a partner using Kenyan school situations.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: When you meet your teacher in the morning, say “Good morning” clearly and smile.

Example 2: Listen to a short instruction, then repeat it to a friend in your own words.

Example 3: Role-play buying an item at the market using polite requests: “Please…”, “Thank you.”

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Practise a 30-second greeting dialogue with a partner.
2. Listen to three instructions and carry them out in order.
3. Tell a short news item from your day using complete sentences.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Teach a younger learner one polite greeting from this lesson.
2. Write five sentences you can say when welcoming a visitor at school.
3. Ask a parent to give you three oral instructions; write them down after listening.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Learners express personal feelings orally
2. Learners are encouraged to participate in using acquired vocabulary speaking competitions to communicate effectively
3. Learners identify good and poor variation, articulation and presentation skills(videos recording of stress to express self- presentations or role playing by teacher) confidently
4. Speaks clearly and audibly, using learnt

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Good listeners look, wait, and respond.
2. Clear speech helps others understand you.
3. Polite language shows respect.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
